hook: Mark Chen has been at OpenAI since 2018, moving from quantitative trading into leading some of the company's most visible research programs. He co-led the team that built DALL-E, directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 its multimodal capabilities, and oversaw Codex, the model behind GitHub Copilot. In March 2025 OpenAI named him Chief Research Officer, a role focused on integrating research and product development so new capabilities move into deployment faster. He also coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team, a pastime that tracks with his own path through competitive mathematics and computer science at MIT.

quick_facts: Chief Research Officer at OpenAI since March 24, 2025.
Joined OpenAI in 2018 after working as a quantitative trader building machine-learning models for futures and equities trading at Jane Street Capital.
Earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics with computer science from MIT, graduating in 2012.
Co-led the team behind DALL-E and directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 image-understanding capability. Also led Codex, the model underlying GitHub Copilot.
Credited on OpenAI's own GPT-4 contributions page as Vision team co-lead and Deployment lead, and on the o1 contributions page under Leadership and Executive Leadership.
Coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team.
